criteria.promise_scope: Crossrail promised that services would commence in December 2018 in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood.
criteria.observed_scope: TfL reports the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood was rescheduled to Autumn 2019, and later reports Elizabeth line operations/opening on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in May 2022.
criteria.explanation: The original undertaking is explicitly dated: "December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood" (c1). A later TfL FOI response states: "The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018" (c2), which directly shows the December 2018 opening did not occur as planned. TfL then reports the Elizabeth line service pattern between Paddington and Abbey Wood (c3) and states the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood had an "opening day" (c4), confirming the service eventually opened, but after the promised date.

trace.label: REFUTED
trace.verdict: The December 2018 commitment is documented, but the evidence directly disproves opening by that date. Crossrail originally promised central services between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood in December 2018, yet TfL states the opening was deferred to Autumn 2019 and later evidence shows the central Elizabeth line section operating only in 2022.
trace.reasoning:
Requested scope: Did London's Elizabeth line open its central passenger service from Paddington to Abbey Wood by the originally planned December 2018 date?

The question asks about actual delivery against the original December 2018 timetable for the central passenger service from Paddington to Abbey Wood. Citation c1 documents the exact commitment and scope. Citation c2 is direct evidence that, before the promised date, the board moved the opening to Autumn 2019, which is incompatible with opening by December 2018. Citations c3 and c4 corroborate that the central service eventually operated/opened between Paddington and Abbey Wood, but they do not salvage the original timing; instead they reinforce that opening occurred later than promised. Therefore the promise is documented, and fulfillment by the promised date is refuted rather than merely unverified.

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “December 2018 — Crossrail services commence in the central tunnel section between Paddington low level and Abbey Wood”
https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/annual-update-on-crossrail-2017

c2: “The Crossrail Ltd Board took the decision to open the central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood in Autumn 2019 on 29 August 2018.”
https://tfl.gov.uk/corporate/transparency/freedom-of-information/foi-request-detail?referenceId=FOI-1470-1819

c3: “The Elizabeth line will operate 12 trains per hour between Paddington and Abbey Wood from Monday to Saturday 06:30 to 23:00.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-elizabeth-line-to-open-on-24-may-2022

c4: “The celebratory response to the opening saw around 260,000 journeys made on the new central section between Paddington and Abbey Wood across its opening day, clearly showing its popularity.”
https://tfl-newsroom.prgloo.com/news/tfl-press-release-celebrations-as-transformational-elizabeth-line-begins-operations
